reading.body:
Accelera Data Systems is not a confirmed data center: the coordinates resolve to a garage door company, and no website, registration, or press coverage exists for the name.

The pattern is a generic name attached to a pin in the Deer Valley area of Phoenix. Reverse geocoding at the stored coordinates returns a different current occupant, an unrelated home-services business at 2501 West Behrend Drive. That leaves two possibilities the record cannot separate: a stale or imprecise map pin, or an address that was vacated. Nothing links this row to the other eight in its batch, which sit 15 to 20 miles away, so there is no shared building to reason from. The entry carries zero megawatts and no published specifications.

For AI capacity accounting this matters because facility inventories are only as good as their weakest entries. Arizona has four facilities with published power figures totaling 512 MW. This entry contributes nothing to that total and cannot be ranked against it. Counting it as a facility would raise the count without adding capacity, and dropping it silently would hide the uncertainty. The defensible state is unconfirmed, which is how it is filed.

What the record does not tell you is whether a data center ever operated at this address, whether one operates now, or whether the name refers to a planned project, a defunct business, or a mapping error. It also cannot supply an operator, a capacity, or a build date. Resolving any of that would require independent sources that this entry does not have.
